structure: Part 9 mined all 15 trace zips its read names, from four spec files in the tests repo's animals project (tests/animals/e2e/features/address-book/), all of which were read in full: address-book-navigation.spec.ts (1: follows the Address book item from the animals journey to the INS address book and back [c4eb9]); addresses-add-handshake.spec.ts (2: saving a new address in INS returns to the picker with it selected and committed [bcd17]; cancelling INS add returns to the picker without saving an address [55254]); addresses-picker.spec.ts (1: the picker searches and pages the address book, and the row selected on a later page is the one that saves [98845]); addresses-read-only.spec.ts (11: per role, Consignor or exporter, Place of origin, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination, 'links to INS to add an address when the full stack is running' [6173e, feeb7, 8b5e4, fd6b1, 8ab82, all passed] and 'offers no INS add link in stub mode' [9a7a6, 20282, 0200a, 1bc3e, c3c13, all skipped after their beforeEach ran]; plus 'the create-address page is no longer served' [9baa5]). The bundled trace viewer refused every zip (TraceVersionError: the traces were recorded by a newer Playwright), so each zip was read from its unzipped copy in this part's work folder with jq: test.trace (test steps, locators and assertions), N-trace.trace (frame snapshots rendered back to HTML) and N-trace.network (resource snapshots, with request and response bodies under resources/). Refs name the trace by its folder hash fragment, then the call id of the snapshot or the request URL. The corpus ran against the compose stack (animals frontend on :3000, INS frontend on :3002, Defra ID stub on :3007, address-book API on :8089), not stub mode, which is why the five stub-mode tests skipped and their traces still show the INS add link. Pages in this slice, in the order a user meets them: (1) the Consignment addresses hub at /live-animals/notifications/{ref}/addresses, mined only for each role row's Add, Change and Edit details links and the value it shows before and after a pick; (2) the address picker, one per role, at /consignors/select, /place-of-origin/select, /consignees/select, /importers/select and /destinations/select: journey strip, caption Consignment parties, the role as h1, a one-line description, an Add a new address link to INS, a Search field with hint, a table of address-book rows each with a small radio and a View details disclosure, a 'Showing 5 of N addresses' caption, GOV.UK pagination at five rows a page, an inset showing the carried selection, and Save and continue; its variants are unfiltered page 1, page 2, searched to one row, searched to two rows, cleared, returned from INS with ?selected=, and re-entered after a save; (3) the Defra ID stub sign-in (Sign in using Government Gateway), met when the journey first crosses to INS; (4) the INS Add address details page at :3002/address-book/add with the handshake query, its fields and its two buttons, saved and cancelled; (5) the animals return endpoint /address-return, seen only as a redirect; (6) the create-address URL /addresses/create?for=consignor, which answers 404 Page not found; (7) the service navigation on both frontends, the INS Address book list at /address-book and the INS Dashboard at /, reached from the Address book item and left by the INS dashboard's Start a new notification link back to /live-animals. Snapshots of the picker itself are missing from two skipped traces (Consignor or exporter 9a7a6 and Place of destination c3c13): their network logs show the picker GET, but the trace closed before a snapshot. What is conditional: the INS add link (compose or CDP only, per the spec; stub mode never traced), the selected-address inset and the selected= parameter on pagination (only when a selection exists), the pagination block (only when results exceed one page), and the hub row actions (Add before a pick, Change and Edit details after). Seeding went straight to the address-book API (POST /organisation/5900001/addresses), so the network logs also show its request and response shape.
